summary: Resolve local explicit-agent conversation ownership once and seek bounded identity and routing history

replay.detail: No claim replay or projection rules change; existing claims supply the same owner and route selections.

schema.detail: Adds 5 indexes: claims_transport_pair_accepted_index, claims_actual_accepted_index, claims_runtime_origin_accepted_index, claims_identity_runtime_id_accepted_index and claims_identity_incarnation_id_accepted_index. claims_runtime_id_subject_index already exists on main and is not new. Existing databases create the indexes on open without a schema version transition; no claims or existing indexes are removed. These indexes are mandatory from this version on: readers use INDEXED BY, so a new build against a store where the required indexes were dropped fails those reads.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; mixed-build members retain the existing replication contract.

compatibility.detail: No client-v0, peer protocol, pairing or harness contract change. The owner-once fix covers local explicit-agent open only. The peer path is NOT covered: a remote-owned explicit-agent open goes through crates/st3-peer/src/peer.rs:1244-1267 to conversation_changes or timeline_value and then managed_session_owner_at (crates/st3-api/src/api.rs:3514-3530), which still uses the fleet owner map. Other remaining global-map callers include conversation_stream (client_v0.rs:8050-8070), conversation_changes (7980-8001), timeline_value (6857-6909) and the native_slice_page fallback (6054-6065). The Fractal first-frame acceptance of <=150 ms cold/warm and the #2436/#2590 sample apply only to the paths this PR fixes: local explicit-agent open. The 150 ms target is not claimed for the peer path; a follow-up PR covers that path. Production first-frame latency remains unmeasured.

downtime.detail: First open of an existing database builds the new indexes before API availability; subsequent opens reuse them. See the production-size copy measurement in #3116, pending tonight: index-build duration and rollout downtime remain unknown until that measurement. If the build exceeds about 5 s, the plan is a pre-rollout maintenance step using the same idempotent DDL, run once before the daemon serves.

manual.detail: No identity migration is required. Whether the pre-rollout index maintenance step is needed depends on the pending production-size copy measurement in #3116; use the same idempotent DDL once before the daemon serves if the build exceeds about 5 s.

recovery.detail: The added indexes do not alter stored claims. Swapping back to an older build leaves the indexes in place harmlessly; older binaries ignore them. Do not drop the required indexes while serving with the new build: its INDEXED BY readers fail if they are absent.
